Document.project_name: Lodge at Bow Lake Contaminated Site Remediation
Document.description: The Lodge at Bow Lake is proposing to remediate contaminated soils from historic fuelling practices at the site between 1970 and 2013. Work will involve the removal of contaminated soils to a licensed landfill, backfilling with clean material and post remediation monitoring.

Document.project_name: New Delivery Centre - Orillia ON
Document.description:
Canada Post Corporation (CPC) is proposing to construct and operate a New Delivery Centre on a 1.31-hectare site at 14-16 Nelle Carter Court in Orillia, Ontario. 

The Project includes a new building of approximately 1,300 square meters.  Pre-construction activities will include exclusion fencing, land clearing, topsoil stripping, sub-excavation, engineered fill, rough grading, and implementation of a soil management plan. The new Delivery Centre is a final sort facility for mail and parcels and will include some office space. The Project site will also include loading and parking spaces for trucks and a trailer, employee parking, landscaping, stormwater management, site lighting, and waste and recycling storage.

Document.project_name: Municipality of Jasper Wastewater Treatment Plant Equalization Pond Reinstatement
Document.description: The Municipality of Jasper Wastewater Treatment Plant has experienced several system failures and service disruptions that resulted in untreated wastewater entering the original lagoon system and subsequently migrating into the underlying rocky substrate. The Municipality of Jasper is proposing to install an appropriate liner system within the existing lagoon cell to provide adequate containment.

Document.project_name: Town of Banff Sulphur Mountain Pipeline and Kootenay Pumphouse Replacement
Document.description: The Town of Banff water services is proposing a new water pipeline to service upper Sulphur Mountain (gondola, hot pools, Rimrock), as well as the replacement of the current pumphouse close to Kootenay Ave. The Town is requesting to install the new watermain adjacent to the existing right of way (ROW) (Fortis Power lines) by widening it permanently by 10 meters (20 m during project, 10 m to be reclaimed afterward). This will allow them to maintain the current water supply to downstream users (PCA, Rimrock, Pursuit), and maintain safe distances from the current ATCO gas line. The pipeline will be installed by open trench for 90% of it's length (the safest method due to other buried utilities), and horizontal directional drilling where open trench is not safe/feasible. The new pipeline will tie into the existing Sulphur Mountain Reservoir located up slope from the PCA Upper Hot Springs. The existing water main will be abandoned in place. The existing Pump Station will be demolished once the new potable main and respective pump station are commissioned. The temporary construction workspace and new pipeline easement will be remediated after completion of pipeline. The Kootenay pump house will be replaced with a new building.

Document.project_name: Wood chip plant remediation - 8501 Ontario Street
location: Wood chip plant remediation - 8501 Ontario Street
Document.description:
Howe Sound Pulp & Paper Corporation (HSPPC) is proposing targeted environmental remediation activities at the former West Coast Chip Plant site located at 8501/8502 Ontario Street, Vancouver. The remediation follows completion of a Detailed Site Investigation (DSI), Detailed Quantitative Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessment (DQHHERA), and Remedial Action Plan (RAP), which identified localized soil and groundwater contamination associated with historical industrial operations. The project is intended to address petroleum hydrocarbons (LEPH/HEPH), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), tetraethyl lead (TEL), localized light non-aqueous phase liquid (LNAPL), and other contaminants through targeted excavation and associated groundwater management.

The proposed works include excavation and off-site disposal of contaminated soils, localized LNAPL recovery, temporary dewatering (if required), confirmatory soil and groundwater sampling, installation of post-remediation monitoring wells, and restoration of excavated areas with clean imported fill. The project also includes decommissioning and removal of the existing stormwater treatment aeration lagoon and associated infrastructure, as well as removal of an associated electrical transformer. Environmental protection measures, including erosion and sediment control, stormwater management, and construction environmental monitoring, will be implemented throughout the remediation program in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

Document.project_name: Maintenance of the dams at Lac à la Pêche and Lac Wapizagonke, La Clairière area
location: La Mauricie National Park of Canada
La Mauricie National Park of Canada
Document.description: The dams at Lac à la Pêche and Lac Wapizagonke (La Clairière sector) require maintenance to ensure their safety and extend their service life. The work includes repairing the caissons and wooden abutments, stabilizing the riprap downstream of the dams and at the shore supports, and controlling vegetation adjacent to and above the abutments and supports.

Document.project_name: Wharf 401 Reconstruction - Millerand Harbour - Magdalen Islands
Document.proponent: Small Craft Harbours  - Fisheries and Oceans Canada
Document.description:
A recent underwater inspection revealed extensive deterioration of exposed wooden com-ponents and bolted assemblies. New cladding or ladders can no longer be safely installed due to the advanced degradation of the existing wood.

Built in 1974, the structure has exceeded its intended lifespan, and partial repairs are no longer viable. A full reconstruction of Wharf 401 is required to ensure the safety of vessels and fishermans.

 
The project includes the following activities:

•    Supply of treated timber, plastic cladding, galvanized hardware, concrete slabs, and ballast stone
•    Partial demolition of the existing creosote treated timber cribwork
•    Proper disposal of demolition materials, including treated and creo-sote contaminated wood
•    Excavation of the seabed to prepare a granular foundation for new cribwork
•    Assembly, launching, placement, and completion of timber cribwork structures
•    Installation of precast concrete slabs, ladders, and fenders
•    Electrical and mechanical upgrades to modernize wharf services

Document.project_name: Fredericton Farm Services Building Replacement Project
Document.description:
Project Description:

Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada intends to build a new 1,326 m2 farm services building and demolish an old 2,060 m2 building at the Fredericton Research and Development Center. The development work will also include: 1. road and parking lot improvements, 2. utility hookups, and 3. building landscaping.

Document.project_name: Shell Beach Erosion Control Project, Portland Island
Document.description: Ongoing monitoring by Parks Canada and First Nations has shown severe erosion at Shell Beach on Portland Island. Parks Canada is proposing a shoreline restoration project to reduce the levels of erosion. The work will involve a soft-armouring approach to dissipate wave action and the revegetation of native plants to further stabilize the shoreline. Parks Canada will complete a basic impact assessment to assess the proposed project's potential impacts to natural and cultural resources. The impact assessment will incorporate standard and site-specific measures to avoid and minimize potential impacts to natural and cultural resources.

Document.project_name: Crown Mountain Coking Coal Project
YYG GSE Area Expansion
Proposed 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet
Document.description:
Construction
The construction of a single storey 477 m2 (5,134 ft2) wood framed commercial building with slab-on-grade foundation. The new commercial building will house two (2) tenants including the Retail Petroleum Outlet with Convenience Store and a quick-service restaurant with drive-thru.

Bio-Physical Environment: A site reconnaissance was conducted on June 10, 2026. The construction and operation are not projected to have any adverse environmental effect.

Human Environment: The proposed 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet is located within the Charlottetown Airport Business Park with a mix of commercial and industrial businesses. The areas immediately adjacent and around the proposed 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet project are vacant commercial business lots at this time.

Operations
The 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet will include Gas Bar and will include the following petroleum storage and dispensing infrastructure:


	100,000 L petroleum underground storage tank (UST)* with 3 section including:
	
		65,000 L regular gasoline product;
		20,000 L diesel product; and
		15,000 L supreme gasoline product.
	
	
	Four (4) Pump Islands with four (4) Dispensers and ten (10) nozzles.


It should be noted that all petroleum infrastructure (i.e., UST, Pump Island, Dispensers etc.) will be constructed and installed to the latest industry standards to be productive of human health and the environment. The new facility will also have a retail propane exchange outlet associated with the convenience store operation. The new commercial building will use propane heat with the quick service restaurant tenant have separate propane tanks for their operations. Operations at the subject site will be connected to the City of Charlottetown municipal systems to supply potable water and sanitary sewer services. The expected volumes of water to be used by the proposed new facility are expected to be minimal.

Mitigation
During the construction phase, stormwater runoff and sediment control measures will be provided by the site contractor and reviewed by the Construction Project Manager on a regular basis. This will include installing silt fencing, straw bales and other measures as required. All construction debris (including any excess site soils) will be disposed of in a provincially approved manner. Any monitoring wells on the proposed expansion footprint would be decommissioned/relocated as required. During construction and operation (including accidents, potential malfunctions and unplanned events) all municipal, provincial and federal codes, standards and best management practices will be followed.

ATCO Pipeline 1165 - Ext (6c) Kainai Community Subdivision
Sanitary Lift Station Upgrades at Royal Military College of Canada
location: Royal Military College of Canada, 20 General Crerar Crescent, Kingston
Document.description: The Sanitary Lift Station at RMCC is in need of replacement to ensure continued function, and to improve the safety of workers that maintain the stations, associated pumps and wells. The proposed project involves removal and replacement of the pump station and wet well, associated underground utility infrastructure, along with upgrades to lift station electrical controls at the RMCC Boathouse building located at 20 General Crerar Crescent. The construction work is planned to begin in autumn 2020.

Document.project_name: Laydown and Logistics areas
Document.description:
The Proposed Project: Laydown and Logistics areas

As part of the Greater Toronto Airports Authority's (GTAA's) Toronto Pearson Airport Longterm Investment in Facilities & Terminals (LIFT) Program, logistics and laydown areas will be constructed on Airport Lands, to facilitate construction needs. The sites will consist of temporary construction trailers, worker parking lot, material laydown, equipment storage, and associated infrastructure to support Airport construction projects.

The sites will undergo a variety of improvements, depending upon the requirements for construction, which are expected to include as required minor excavation, clearing and grubbing, utility removals/relocations including the addition of temporary pole-mounted lighting with overhead power, re-grading, placement of aggregate and compact areas where required, construction trailers, security booths, transportation services for workers, paving and line painting of parking and trailer areas, stormwater management, and other associated infrastructure. No new permanent buildings are proposed. Trailers will be prefabricated units delivered to the site.

Several sustainability best practices will be incorporated into the projects design and implementation for the wider Toronto Pearson Airport Longterm Investment in Facilities & Terminals (LIFT) Program.

Document.project_name: Temporary Laydown and Logistics Area
Warkworth Institution – Fuel Storage Tank System Replacements and Removals (8)
Document.description: Correctional Service Canada requires the removal and replacement of five (5) fuel storage tanks at the Warkworth Institution site as well as three (3) additional fuel tank systems require removal with no replacements contemplated. The tanks are all greater than 20 years old and deteriorating. The existing tanks on-site are concrete encased petroleum fuel storage tanks. The project will entail decommissioning and removal of the existing tanks, design of tanks and product transfer areas, and installation of new tank systems.

Document.project_name: Yellowhead Copper Project
Document.description:
Trekor Metals Limited is proposing the construction, operation, and closure of a new open-pit copper mine located about 150 kilometres northeast of Kamloops, British Columbia. The Yellowhead Copper Project has been designed with a production capacity of 90,000 tonnes of ore per day (up to 32 million tonnes per year) over a 25-year mine life. The project, which would also produce gold and silver, includes a new mill, an approximately 110 kilometre transmission line that would connect to an existing B.C. Hydro substation near 100 Mile House, and a rail load-out facility at an existing site at Vavenby.

British Columbia's Environmental Assessment Office is collaborating with the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada as part of the federal impact assessment of the project. For more information on the EAO's process, please visit EPIC.engage.

 

Please note that the proponent of this project was previously known as Taseko Mines Limited.

Document.project_name: Fort Frontenac Storm Drainage and Parking Lot Reconstruction Project
Document.description: The Fort Frontenac Storm Drainage and Parking Lot Reconstruction project involves replacing and repairing site infrastructure to manage the stormwater within Fort Frontenac, in Kingston, Ontario. The work includes replacement/upsizing of existing portions of the storm sewers, installing new storm systems, new outfall, abandoning existing service connections and reconstructing the parking lot to address site drainage issues. The project also includes spot repairs to the sanitary sewer prior to new asphalt reinstatement, replacement of impacted curbs and sidewalks, addressing utility conflicts, removal of the abandoned tennis court, improved Fort access/egress and parking. The project is required to bring the site infrastructure in line with typical quantity and quality control best management practices to help mitigate the negative impacts of surface flooding and high Lake Ontario water levels, help to preserve the historic infrastructure assets in Fort Frontenac.

Document.project_name: Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) and Roof Refit - CFB Kingston
location: CFB Kingston, 6 Red Patch Avenue, Kingston
Document.description:
The project involves retrofitting the roof and relocating the HVAC units.

Building MC39 is a pre-engineered, single storey steel building constructed circa 1990 with a with a gross floor area of 3,406 m2. There are currently nine (9) rooftop HVAC units and associated condensers on a standing seam metal roof. The condensers are supported by the platform structure that runs the length of the building, while the HVAC units sit on roof curbs. There are roof leaks around the roof penetrations for both the platform legs and roof curbing.

All existing HVAC units and associated condensers will be decommissioned and permanently removed from the roof. New HVAC units will be installed on the north side of the building on grated steel structures with pillars. Each pillar will be augured and the excess soil will be spread around the site for reuse and restoration. The existing standing seam metal roof will be replaced with a new one.

Document.project_name: Pikangikum First Nation - Short Term Water and Wastewater Upgrades
Saskatoon Airport Authority - Firehall Renovation and Expansion
CFB Kingston Energy Conservation Project
location: Brockville Armoury 144 King St. East Brockville
Document.description:
This project consists of work execution, labour, materials/supplies and tools needed for the improvement of the energy efficiency of the Canadian Forces Base Kingston real property, with measures to lower greenhouse gas emissions.

The work includes but is not limited to:

• Replacement of lighting systems with Light Emitting Diode (LED) lights, fixtures, and controls.

• Upgrading controls on existing and new environmental systems.

• Installation of variable frequency drives (VFD) on fans.

• Piping insulation on heated and chilled water piping.

• Installation of water efficient plumbing fixtures including flow restrictors.

• Window replacement to maximize energy retention.

• Improvement of building envelope air sealing.

• Replacement of rooftop heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) units.

• Replacement of hot water boiler systems with gas-fired condensing boilers.

• Leak detection and repair, and sub-metering for water savings.

• Installation of natural gas generators, ground-mounted Photovoltaic (PV) panels and a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) to reduce peak demand for energy.

• Optimisation of the mechanical systems of HVAC equipment through replacement and installation of an Energy Management System.

• Summer shut down of the Central Heating Plant.

• Replacement of steam traps and pipe insulations in mechanical rooms.

• Replacement of the Dome exterior fabric, ventilation and heating systems.

Some of the work will produce construction residue that will be disposed of in conformity with ongoing environmental regulations.

The project is led by the Department of National Defence. The project will affect roughly sixty buildings. It will be located inside a developed area both inside and outside the controlled zone of Canadian Forces Base Kingston, in the city of Kingston (Ontario). Other buildings are located on satellite sites; Kingston Armoury, Kingston (Ontario) and Brockville Armoury, Brockville (Ontario).

Document.project_name: Joyce Lake Direct Shipping Iron Ore Project
location: Labrador (approximately 20 km northeast of Schefferville, QC)
Document.description:
Joyce Direct Iron Inc. is proposing the construction, operation and decommissioning of an open-pit iron ore mine located in Newfoundland and Labrador, approximately 20 kilometres northeast of Schefferville, Quebec. As proposed, the mine would produce up to an estimated 2.5 million tons of ore per year over a life span of seven years. The project would consist of an open pit mine, dewatering of Joyce Lake, crushing and screening of ore (dry processing), waste rock disposal, support infrastructure, access and haulage roads, a causeway, and a rail loop to connect with an existing railway.

Please note that the proponent for this project was formerly Labec Century Iron Ore Inc.

Document.project_name: DND New Gravel Parking Pad - 3701 Carling Avenue - Ottawa, Ontario
Document.description: The scope of work will consist of building a 43 meter by 30 meter (approximately) gravel pad. This would involve excavating 18 inches of topsoil, installing a Geotech fabric layer, placing 12 inches of granular B topped with 6 inches of granular, and then compacted.

Document.project_name: Reconstruction of a section of the Anse-à-Beaufils wharf
Document.description:
The port of L'Anse-à-Beaufils is located on the south side of the Gaspé Peninsula. This harbour is the home port of 16 commercial fishing vessels and is owned by Fisheries and Oceans Canada. Pier 401, built in 1980, is affected by severe pile corrosion and deterioration of the concrete panels. As a result, Pier 410 must be rebuilt over a length of approximately 70 m.

The proposed concept is the reconstruction of a Berliner wall anchored directly to the façade of the existing wall. This minimizes fish habitat loss and avoids the complete demolition of the existing wharf. Since this portion of the wharf is located between the boat launch and a section of wharf made of steel sheet piles, the connection of the new structure will be carried out in a harmonious manner.  The reconstruction of this structure is essential to maintain the operational capacity of the port.

Document.project_name: Artillery Storage Shed, Halifax Citadel National Historic Site
Document.description: The purpose of this project is to establish a purpose-built, on-site winter storage facility to eliminate the logistical challenges associated with the current off-site storage arrangement. The installation of a prefabricated storage structures (sea containers) within the Halifax Citadel ditch would be completed to provide a secure, winter storage for field guns, swivel guns, and related equipment. The facility would be equipped with electrical service, insulation, and heating to protect artifacts and equipment from winter conditions. The structures will be supported on a gravel pad foundation, minimizing site disturbance.

The project will improve operational efficiency, provide dedicated handwashing and cleaning option within the Carpentry Shop, and re-establish water service to the Garage for vehicle washing. The proposed work includes installation of water supply lines from Visitors Quarters (Vis Q), a utility sink and on demand water heater in the Carpentry Shop, a small wastewater disposal system for sink drainage, and a heated enclosure to protect pressure-washing equipment in the Garage during winter operations.

Document.project_name: Ermineskin Cree Nation On-Reserve Water Supply Project
Document.description:
Ermineskin Cree Nation is proposing to construct Phase I of an On-Reserve Water Supply Project. The project will include the construction of 1.3 km of waterline from the Nation boundary to a new water reservoir and pump station and the dormancy of 6 existing groundwater well.

The project is largely contiguous to existing linear infrastructure and the pipeline will be installed using a trench method. The project will cross up to 4 temporary graminoid marsh wetlands. There are no known or suspected contaminated sites within the project footprint

No species at risk have been identified, no critical habitat in proximity of the proposed project, and construction activities will take place outside of the migratory bird period of April 15 to August 31. There are no known or suspected contaminated sites within the project footprint.

Indigenous Services Canada is providing funding for the project.

Document.project_name: One Arrow First Nation Subdivision Project
Document.description: The proposed subdivision development project will consist of construction of 54 lots, encompassing approximately 15 ha of land. The development will require underground utility installations, site roadways and ditching, and lot grading. The proposed site is located immediately north of an existing subdivision, to which the proposed subdivision roadways would connect with. Erosion control measures will be implemented as required during construction until adequate vegetative growth has re-established. Topsoil will be stripped from all development areas and will be temporarily stockpiled for the duration of construction. Following completion of excavation works, the topsoil will be replaced and the area will be reseeded. All anticipated waste generated during construction activities will be responsibly managed and disposed of at designated landfill facility. In addition, procedures will be implemented throughout construction to prevent potential contamination from petroleum products used for on-site equipment.

Document.project_name: Taza Park West Self Storage Facility
Document.description: StoreWest is proposing to construct a self-storage facility at Tsuut'ina Nation. The proposed project will be located at Taza Park West near the intersection of Glenmore Trail and Tsuut'ina Trail. The proposed project will include the construction of a three story self-storage building with a footprint of  3,959 meters squared, loading bays, a nine stall parking lot, an access road, and a landscaped amenity area. The project will be built on a pre-graded site with utilities already installed. Project activities include re-grading, construction of the total precast concrete building, installation of subbase and asphalt, and landscaping. The project is not expected to impact any waterbodies, migratory birds, or species at risk.

Document.project_name: Fire Hall 27 Demolition
Document.description: Lot MK.13 at the Calgary International Airport currently houses a 1960's two-storey 7200 sqft. Building T042 (old Fire Hall 27) that is slated for demolition. The project will disconnect, decommission, cap, mark, and where necessary, remove all utilities including electricity, gas, sanitary, and water lines at the closest t-junction / manhole / junction box adjacent to the building within the property line and remove and dispose of the existing building, including any hazardous materials, as well as all structures above-grade, any and all below-grade footings, foundations, slabs and all waste.  The residual area will be backfilled to provide a safe, flat, level surface at-grade and make good capping to match area outside building footprint on both sides of primary security line (PSL). New PSL fencing will be installed to maintain secure air-side operations. No further improvements or uses of the land are planned for under this project.

Document.project_name: Jasper Park Lodge Wellness Area Development & Trail 4a Refurbishment
Document.description: The Fairmont Jasper Park Lodge is proposing to redevelop one of their Sundeck locations and complete upgrades to Trail 4a directly adjacent to Lac Beauvert and South of their Main Lodge Building. Project activities will include work within the Riparian Zone (changes to trail surface materials, grading/levelling, installation of permanent structures) as well as the introduction of a year-round sauna/cold plunge experience. This project permanently alters the purpose of the Sundeck and associated dock, increases visitor capacity of the offering by providing it year-round, and permanently expanding the physical work associated with this offer within the Riparian Zone. As such, a Basic Impact Assessment will be required.

Document.project_name: Extension of Basile McDougall Street and preparation for housing development - Abitibiwinni
Document.proponent: Council of the First Nation of Abitibiwinni
Document.description:
The project is located in the community of Pikogan. It consists of extending Basile McDougall street to allow urban development, including the addition of residential lots. The street will be extended by approximately 500 meters. The installation of underground infrastructures to manage stormwater, sanitary water and drinking water is also part of the project. Here are the main activities planned as part of the project:

- Installation of typical road infrastructure (e.g. intersections, paving, etc.)

- Installation of typical underground infrastructure (e.g. storm water pipes, sanitary water pipes, etc.)

- Levelling of adjoining lots in preparation for residential construction

- General landscaping

Document.project_name: Regional Assessment in the Ring of Fire Area
Document.description:
The regional assessment will be conducted in the area centred on the Ring of Fire mineral deposits in northern Ontario, approximately 540 kilometres northeast of Thunder Bay. The regional assessment aims to gather information and data on the region; understand potential effects from past, existing and future development in the Ring of Fire area; and will inform and improve future impact assessments. Indigenous partners and the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada are co-leading the regional assessment and will provide Indigenous communities and organizations, federal and provincial governments, non-government organizations and the public opportunities to meaningfully participate.

Indigenous partners include: Aroland First Nation, Attawapiskat First Nation, Constance Lake First Nation, Eabametoong First Nation, Fort Albany First Nation, Ginoogaming First Nation, Kashechewan First Nation, Long Lake #58 First Nation, Marten Falls First Nation, Missanabie Cree First Nation, Moose Cree First Nation, Neskantaga First Nation, Nibinamik First Nation, Webequie First Nation, and Weenusk First Nation. Administrative support is provided by the Matawa and Mushkegowuk Councils.

To support engagement and information sharing, an Information Sharing Platform (ISP) has been developed for this assessment. The ISP offers additional tools to explore geospatial data through interactive maps, visual summaries and storytelling tools, and thematic content.

Document.description: Sitansisk is experience a housing shortage and have conducted a feasibility study examining potential properties suitable for future housing development. Sitansisk is proceeding with plans to construct a housing development for up to 30 lots on approximately 3 hectares of land.  Activities include clearing, grubbing, and grading of the development area, new roadways, ditches, water and wastewater services and stormwater ponds to manage storm water.

Document.project_name: Settlers Road Widening
Document.description: The proposed project will widen the single-lane section to accommodate two-lane traffic. As well, widen two nearby sections of road to improve the line of site and road safety. The project location is between kilometre five and six and begins at approximately 50°40'6.72"N 115°51'14.87"W. The scope of work includes tree and vegetation removal, slope excavation, and debris removal.

Document.project_name: Moosomin First Nation Landfill Decommissioning
Document.description: Moosomin First Nation is proposing to conduct landfill decommissioning and reclamation of the historical dumpsite located in SW-32-47-16-W3M. Decommissioning activities will start with removing contaminated soil from mixed waste dioxins and furans from the impacted borehole site and deliver contaminated soil to appropriate facility. Following the removal of the contaminated material,  site preparation will include removing any metal, oil cans, shingles and other non-inert waste and moving any inert waste into the existing cells. Site will then be graded and contoured to ensure 3:1 slope of the material in each of the cells.  A 500 mm layer of clay will be placed and compacted over each of the two cells. A 150 mm layer of topsoil will then be placed over the clay cap followed by a native grass seed. Access to the site will be managed by placing soil mounds at the entrance of the site.

Document.project_name: Ochapowace Nation Landfill Decommissioning
Document.description: Ochapowace Nation is proposing to conduct landfill decommissioning and reclamation of the historical dumpsite located in NW 32-17-03-W2M. Decommissioning activities will start with site preparation which includes removing any metal, oil cans, shingles and other non-inert waste and moving any inert waste into the existing cells. Site will then be graded and contoured to ensure 3:1 slope of the material in each of the cells.  A 500 mm layer of clay will be placed and compacted over each of the two cells. A 150 mm layer of topsoil will then be placed over the clay cap followed by a native grass seed.

Document.project_name: North Corridor Expansion Project
Document.description: NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd. (NGTL) is applying to the National Energy Board under section 52 of the National Energy Board Act for approval to construct and operate the North Corridor Expansion Project (the Project) in Alberta.  The Project consists of three natural gas pipelines: two sections of 1,219 mm (nominal pipe size 48 inch), including the 24 km long North Star Section 2 and the 32 km long Red Earth Section 3, and a third section of 1,219 mm (nominal pipe size 36 inch) which is 25 km long and called the Bear Canyon North Extension on the Northwest Mainline Loop No.2.  The Project also includes a unit addition at Hidden Lake North Compressor Station and launcher and receiver facilities for cleaning and in-line inspection. Temporary infrastructure required for construction could include temporary access roads, borrow pits/dugouts, slurry pits, stockpile sites, laydown yards, contractor yards and construction camps. The Project will cross 6 watercourses located in the Peace River Basin; named watercourses include the Notikewin River, Loon River, Hunt Creek, and Bear Canyon Creek. NGTL is proposing to commence construction at the compressor station in November 2019 and commence all three pipeline sections from September 2021 to April 2022.

Document.project_name: Edson Mainline Expansion Project
Document.description: NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd. (NGTL) is applying to the National Energy Board under section 52 of the National Energy Board Act for approval to construct and operate the Edson Mainline Expansion Project (the Project) in Alberta.  The Project consists of two sections of 1,219 mm (nominal pipe size 48) natural gas pipeline, including the 40.2 km long Elk River Section and the 44.7 km long Alford Creek Section, and associated facilities.  The associated facilities include three mainline block valves, one control valve and bypass assembly, ten crossover valves, a receiver facility, and temporary access roads.  The Project will cross 31 watercourses located in the North Saskatchewan River watershed, notably the Brazeau River, Nordegg River, Elk River, Prairie Creek, and the Clearwater River.  NGTL is proposing to construct both pipeline sections from November 2021 to April 2022.

Document.project_name: NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd. - 2021 NGTL System Expansion Project
Document.description:
NOVA Gas Transmission Limited (NGTL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Trans Canada, has filed an application for the 2021 NGTL System Expansion Project. NGTL proposes to build and operate approximately 344 km of 1,219 mm (NPS 48) outside diameter natural gas pipeline and associated facilities in northwestern Alberta. If approved, the project would "loop" or add new pipeline parallel or adjacent to, the existing NGTL System.

The Project includes three main areas:

Grande Prairie West Area:


	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 4 (Valhalla Section), approximately 36 km; and,
	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 3 (Elmworth Section), approximately 46 km.


Grande Prairie South Area:


	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 2 (Karr Section), approximately 57 km;
	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 2 (Deep Valley Section), approximately 69 km; and,
	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 2 (McLeod River Connection Section), approximately 14 km.


Edson South Area:


	Edson Mainline Loop No. 4 (Rob Section), approximately 42 km;
	Edson Mainline Loop No. 4 (Dismal Creek Section), approximately 32 km;
	Edson Mainline Loop 4 (Brewer Section), approximately 49 km;
	Three compressor station unit additions at Nordegg, AB, Didsbury, AB and Beiseker, AB; and,
	January Creek Control Valve and associated pipeline tie-ins.


In its application, NGTL said the project was needed to transport natural gas from areas of increasing production in northwestern Alberta and northeastern BC to intra-Alberta and export markets. If approved, NGTL plans to begin operating the project by April 2021.

The application includes designated physical activities listed in the Regulations Designating Physical Activities (Regulations) under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012 (CEAA 2012), specifically the construction of over 40 km of new pipeline. As a result, the Project will be a designated project for the purposes of CEAA 2012 for which the NEB will be the responsible authority.

Document.project_name: Cold Lake First Nation: CUZ46 Wastewater System Expansion
Document.description:
The existing capacity of the Cold Lake First Nation wastewater collection and treatment system has been deemed insufficient to meet current and projected future demand. As such, Cold Lake First Nation proposes the expansion of its wastewater collection infrastructure to include an expansion of the collection system, and construction of a new lift station, 4.4 km of wastewater forcemain and gravity wastewater main, connection to the City of Cold Lake wastewater collection and treatment infrastructure, and decommissioning of the existing Cold Lake First Nation wastewater treatment lagoon. The on-reserve portions of the routing will generally follow established roadways to the crossing of the Beaver River.

     Extensive geohazard analysis and geotechnical investigations have been completed and identified the presence of a deep-seated landslide along the south embankment of the Beaver River. Trees within the landslide area suggest that the slope has not been subject to significant displacement for at least 50 years indicating stability of the area in comparison to other alignments reviewed as part of the project. The north side of the river valley does not demonstrate significant geohazards.

     Vegetation will be cleared and mulched to a width of 4.0m along the entire route to facilitate equipment access and maintenance of the infrastructure.

     The off-reserve alignments generally follow un-developed public right-of-ways under the jurisdiction of the MD of Bonnyville and are outside of the scope of this impact assessment.
